messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Mostly, yes. What matters most is a fair financial share for me, and that B is properly included; I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I haven’t agreed to it. I don’t want to hurt my twin, but I also don’t want to be pressured into a deal. And yes, being able to say no without it becoming a problem matters.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. It matters because having a secure home would support our financial independence and well-being. I’m uneasy because C hasn’t agreed, and we can’t proceed without her agreement. Your aim sounds reasonable to me.

I’d be grateful if the house could leave me with some money to start a dance studio; that would mean a lot to me. I’m a little uneasy about being hurried into a plan before everyone’s had a chance to speak. And yes, being able to say no without it causing trouble seems important.
All three fit. “Fair share” and “not giving part away without choosing to” are right. I do want to stand up for myself without damaging things with A.
Yes, both statements fit. And yes, it matters that no one’s view gets sidelined because they answer more slowly.

Yes, both fit. I’d make the first a little more direct: “I’d like some money from Dad’s estate to help me start a dance studio.” And I do see the point of not settling things based on who replies fastest.

None is a yes from me. D1 assumes A buys and that valuation settles what’s fair; it doesn’t ensure everyone freely agrees. D2’s instalments make me uneasy unless timing and security are clear. D3 doesn’t ensure A gets a secure home, and the shares depend on the will. D4 is sensible for now, but doesn’t resolve anything. I’m not in a hurry, and I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase.

D1 doesn’t reflect my wish to buy at a family discount. D2 is closest to what I hope for, but only if C genuinely agrees; the details still need advice. D3 isn’t my preferred outcome. D4 seems sensible for now. I can’t say whether the others have discomfort, and none of these drafts settles B’s studio plans or all the details of C’s fairness concerns.

I can’t tell whether D1 or D3 would give me enough to start the studio until my share is clear. D4 leaves that unresolved, though I understand why it keeps things open. I’m a little uncomfortable with instalments in D2; the money would need to be available when I’m ready to start.

D5 is fine as a next step, provided the valuation and advice don’t commit anyone to a sale. D6 is fair to ask A. I’d rather not rule out options in advance, but I won’t subsidize a discount. No other discomfort.

D5 sits right with me as a way to keep things open, not a commitment. D6 is fair. The discount matters as a way to make buying manageable and support our independence; I don’t know whether a full-price mortgage would work for us. No other discomfort comes to mind.
D5 seems sensible. I’m a little uneasy about setting timing before I know what my share might be. “Money available to me when I’m ready” is accurate.
Yes, that fits. B should know what her share is likely to be before anyone asks her to commit to timing.
Understood. I’m comfortable keeping the discount as one option, with nothing decided until we have the advice and valuation and everyone agrees.
Yes, that wording is right. I’d like to know what my share is likely to be before discussing timing.
That’s accurate. Nothing else to add.
That reflects my position. Thanks for keeping the discount as an option, not an assumption.
That reflects what I’ve said. Thank you for keeping my need for studio money and the order of things clear.
